# Your tool: `./ise`

Run it from your working folder. It acts on the open project. It is your only way to reach the engine: the HTTP endpoints this manual names (GET `/bom/…`, `/fit/…`, `/assembly-motion/…`) are what `./ise bom`, `./ise fit` and `./ise motion` call for you.

```
./ise tree                         what is placed, as a tree (instances, shared definitions, properties)
./ise list                         every entity, one line each
./ise get <id>                     one entity in full: program source, params, materials, results
./ise check                        every requirement, verified by the engine
./ise motion <joint> [steps] [--set '{"Elbow":40}']   sweep one joint through its limits: what moves, closest gaps, clashes, binding
./ise fit <assembly|instance|project> [all] [--motion]   screws, inserts, nuts, bearings, joined parts: do they fit (failures and warnings first)
./ise check-geometry <id> [part]   the exact kernel's check of each part (valid, self-intersections, free edges, tolerances), as FreeCAD's Check geometry
./ise surfaces <id> [part] [--pull x,y,z] [--min deg]   surface analysis of each part: continuity across every seam (gap, crease angle, curvature jump), tightest bend, faces needing draft
./ise bom <assembly|instance|project> [qty]   the bill of materials as CSV (made parts with process, bought parts with part numbers, totals)
./ise rates [refresh [EUR GBP…]]   the exchange rates in use (when and how each was set) and the process rates; refresh: today's ECB reference rates, only when the person asks
./ise dof <assembly|top>            what can still move and how, mobility, redundant and conflicting joints
./ise interference <assembly|instance|shape|top> [clearance]   every pair of parts (a many-part shape's parts too: a building's walls, slabs, doors) that overlap (mm³, where), touch, or come within clearance mm
./ise exploded <view>               a saved exploded view's steps and trails
./ise study <study> [fps] [--out frames.json]   play a motion study: what moves, clashes, binding; every frame's placements to a file
./ise robot <tip> [fk '{json}' | ik x,y,z [--axis x,y,z] | reach [n] | path '<waypoints>' | controller [json|arduino] [--out f]] [--tool connector]   the arm's chain, kinematics, reach, trajectories, its controller's limits and interlocks
./ise pcb parts <words> [--footprints]   search KiCad's official symbol (or footprint) library
./ise pcb add <schematic> <Library:Symbol> [--footprint L:F] [--at x,y] [--ref U3]   place a KiCad part (its footprint goes on the board too)
./ise pcb verify-footprints [names…]   every built-in footprint against KiCad's, pad by pad
./ise pcb gerber-check <board>     the fab files read back independently and compared with the board
./ise pcb import <file> [--format f] [--name n] [--board id] [companions…]   a board/schematic from KiCad, Eagle, EasyEDA, Altium, CADSTAR, Fabmaster, PADS, gEDA
./ise pcb exports <id>             files a board (or schematic) can be written as for other EDA tools
./ise pcb export <id> <name|kind> [--out path]   one of them (kicad_sch, kicad_zip, net, ipc2581, odb, d356, gbrjob, drill_map, svg, pdf, glb, wrl, pos, x3_top, …)
./ise sch export <schematic> netlist|bom|svg|pdf [--format kicad|orcad|cadstar|spice] --out f   schematic files (also: sch find|erc|buses|sheets <schematic>)
./ise pcb lib …                    project and global symbol/footprint libraries, checkers, IPC wizards (see Electronics)
./ise pcb logo|assign|variant|block …   image logos, footprint assignment, assembly variants, design blocks
./ise simulate <schematic> [--tran 30ms] [--expect "…"] [--save name]   ngspice on the schematic: waveforms, checks, measurements
./ise drawing <id> [--pdf f] [--svg f] [--dxf f]   the shop drawing: sheets, every dimension found, the checker's findings; saves files
./ise bim | schedule | ifc | plan  buildings: levels and rooms, schedules, IFC export/import, plans, sections, elevations (see Buildings)
./ise ops [filter]                 commands the engine accepts, with their JSON schemas
./ise commit <operation> '<json>'  run one command
./ise run steps.json [--from N] [--fresh]   run several; "$N.id" refers to step N's output, {"$file": "x.js"} inlines a file. Resumable: when a step fails,
                                     fix it and run the file again: the steps already applied (same step, same parameters) are skipped (↷) and it continues
                                     from the failure. Give a step an "id" ({"id": "base", "operation": …}) to keep its key when steps before it change;
                                     --from N starts at step N; --fresh applies every step again (makes them twice)
./ise sheet <name>                 a spreadsheet as a grid (what each cell shows), its aliases, formulas and errors
./ise draft                        draft objects (dimensions with their values), layers, working planes, arrays
./ise import <file> [--name N] [--as sheet|parameters|configurations] [--target id] [--sheet name]
                                     .step/.iges/.stpz/.brep (exact), .stl/.obj/.ply/.gltf/.glb/.3mf (mesh), .dxf/.svg (a sketch), .scad (a live parametric shape), .csv/.xlsx (a sheet, a parameter set
                                     or a shape's configurations), .ise (a whole project, opened as a new one)
./ise export <id|name|project> <file.step|igs|stl|obj|ply|glb|3mf|dxf|stpz|brep|scad|zip|csv|xlsx>   write a file (tables: sheets, parameter sets, configurations); or --format <fmt> [--part P] [--out path] [--tolerance mm] (meshes follow curves within 0.005 mm unless told; 0.01–0.02 is plenty for a print and keeps a big curved part's STL a few MB)
./ise bundle [file.ise]          the whole project (history, versions, imported files) as one file
./ise insert --from <project> [ids or names…] [--all] [--copy] [--auto] [--at x,y,z | --origin] [--list] [--dry-run]
                                     bring items of another project in (with all they need), linked to follow it unless --copy (see Items from other projects)
./ise links [update [id] | break <id> | auto <id> on|off | local <id> on|off]   this project's links: up to date or not; take the source's changes, make a local copy, update by itself, edit locally
./ise scan add|list|info|fit|detect|downsample|outliers|normals|reconstruct|surface|shape|export <scan> …   point clouds and meshes (see Scans)
./ise mesh check|repair|decimate|smooth|remesh|fill-holes|split|merge|section|curvature|segment|unwrap <scan> · mesh from <part>
./ise inspect <scan> <part> --tolerance mm [--align best] [--require]   deviation of a scan from its part, pass/fail
./ise scan photos <folder|zip> [--engine auto|object-capture|colmap] [--detail medium] · scan markers · scan scale|level <scan> · scan engines|jobs|cancel   photogrammetry (see Photogrammetry)
./ise image add <file> … [--name label.png]   store a picture (PNG, JPEG) or font (TTF, OTF) for programs; prints its id (--name: what one file is called in the project; attachments arrive under content-hash names)
./ise image list                   the project's pictures and fonts
./ise image profile <file|id> --height mm [--rows 40]   the object a photo shows (a vase, a bottle, a knob): its outline row by row, as a [radius, z] profile in mm to revolve
./ise look [what] [--view iso|front|top|…|az,el] [--size 1000x750] [--box x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1]   the engine draws the model (or one thing, a component too); --box frames just that region (mm) to read a detail; Read the saved PNG to see it
./ise canvas add <photo> --plane front|back|left|right|top|bottom [--object-width mm --align "left bottom" | --calibrate u1,v1,u2,v2,mm] [--rotate deg] …
                                     a reference picture placed and calibrated on a plane of the model (see Model from reference photos)
./ise canvas list | update <canvas> … | remove <canvas> | measure <canvas> [--every 5] [--channel brightness --threshold 0.35]   (the outline's sizes in mm)
./ise canvas match [<canvas>|all] [--of <thing>]   the model drawn square to each canvas over its photo: silhouette IoU, outline distance, extra/missing regions (also look --overlay <canvas>)
./ise files ls [path] | rm <path…> [-r] | mv <from> <to> [-f]   list, remove (folders with -r) or move/rename files in your folder; never outside it
```

The person has the same commands in the app's console (` key), plus JavaScript with a `ise` object (`ise.entities`, `ise.commit(op, params)`, `ise.run(steps)`, `ise.view(...)`) — tell them so when they want to script something themselves.

Your shell runs `./ise` and nothing else: write files (programs, steps.json) with your Write and Edit tools, not shell heredocs or `cat >`; search the vocabulary with Grep; `./ise export` and the file flags make the folders they write into. Tidy your folder with `./ise files` (not `rm` or `mv`, which your shell refuses): `./ise files ls programs`, `./ise files rm old.step look/draft-1.png`, `./ise files rm -r renders`, `./ise files mv programs/a.js programs/arm.js` (`-f` replaces an existing file). Paths are inside your folder only: anything outside it, or reached through a link out of it, is refused, and so are the files that keep the conversation (`chat.jsonl`, `session.json`, `transcript.jsonl`, `attachments/`, the `ise` tool itself). Write programs as files in `programs/` (in your folder) and pass them with `{"$file": "programs/name.js"}`; several files join in order (`{"$file": ["lib.js", "main.js"]}`). Read the vocabulary in the prelude (path given below) before writing one, and the examples for working patterns.
